### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, touching **22** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**35** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 71696121a64d8bd057fac969a72a84295890ed37`.

⛔ **12** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **35** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 71696121a64d8bd057fac969a72a84295890ed37` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `32c016a1ec3832a25423d5beb542b35c73da9547` — the merge of head `791db71c37806719de5ba66281186385cc0a0100` into base `71696121a64d8bd057fac969a72a84295890ed37`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 32c016a1ec3832a25423d5beb542b35c73da9547 && git checkout 32c016a1ec3832a25423d5beb542b35c73da9547
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 71696121a64d8bd057fac969a72a84295890ed37 791db71c37806719de5ba66281186385cc0a0100 && git checkout -B drift-repro 71696121a64d8bd057fac969a72a84295890ed37 && git merge --no-ff 791db71c37806719de5ba66281186385cc0a0100

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 71696121a64d8bd057fac969a72a84295890ed37
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 71696121a64d8bd057fac969a72a84295890ed37` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `4fb9afa11c69c5542591f1cc16f93725c24cf85e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/mail-log-body-migration.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/mail-log-body-migration.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/index.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/audit-mail-bodies.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/audit-mail-bodies.archive.integration.test.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/schema-migrate.ts; read to judge them: packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/mail-log-body-mask.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/audit/mail-log-body.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/objects/sys-audit-log.object.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/objects/sys-activity.object.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/package.json, packages/spec/src/contracts/data-driver.ts, packages/spec/src/data/driver.zod.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts, packages/types/src/driver-error-classification.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/lifecycle/lifecycle-service.ts, packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts, packages/runtime/src/driver-plugin.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-connection-service.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-admin-plugin.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/one-shot-exit.ts, packages/cli/bin/run.js, packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/plan.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/apply.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/unmapped-columns.ts, scripts/tenant-audit-census.mjs, scripts/check-tenant-audit-census.mjs, .github/workflows/lint.yml, AGENTS.md

This is a read-only review of the head, read in a detached worktree that was removed afterwards. It covers the full diff from merge-base `81e6edd46` to the head: 10 files, +785/−66, in 10 commits. It also covers card #24899 with its claim 6293910100, amendments 6295968920 and 6296052814, and os-dev-report 6295884727; the PR body, including the two Acceptance notes the seat asked to have judged; and the head's check-runs and its two in-progress check-suites. Nothing was built, tested or re-gated, and nothing was written to GitHub. No mail body value, link, token, address or fixture string appears in this record: body columns are named by field and rows are referred to by count.

### ① Derived judgments

**1. Archive mask correctness**

- **Selection and mask value: correct.**
  - Both runners share one loop, `runMailLogBodyCopies` (mail-log-body-migration.ts:258-339).
  - Each page reads only `object_name $in MAIL_LOG_OBJECTS` (:284). That list is exactly `sys_email` and `sys_identity_email` (platform-objects/src/audit/mail-log-body.ts:22).
  - The planner re-checks the object name through `maskMailLogBodyCopy` (mail-log-body-mask.ts:29-30). So no other object's row can be patched, even by a driver that ignored the filter.
  - The masked keys are `MAIL_LOG_BODY_FIELDS`, which is `body_text` and `body_html` (mail-log-body.ts:25). A set body becomes `SECRET_MASK`, null stays null, and an absent key is never invented (mail-log-body-mask.ts:32-37).
  - The writer's `ledgerView` calls the same helper (audit-writers.ts:1774). The writer, the hot runner and the archive runner therefore produce one mask value.
- **Columns walked: complete.**
  - The runner walks `new_value` and `old_value` (mail-log-body-migration.ts:115). These are the writer's two copy columns (audit-writers.ts:2045-2046).
  - The writer also writes `metadata` on an audit row, but only attribution goes there (:2077-2081). So no copy column is missed.
  - Both copy columns are `textarea` (sys-audit-log.object.ts:383, :391), so a driver returns strings and the string-only planner (:94) is not bypassed.
  - The writer's `safeStringify` is plain `JSON.stringify` (audit-writers.ts:520-522), so no stored copy is truncated into text the planner cannot parse.
- **Every other archived column stays byte-identical, `updated_at` included.**
  - The archive write is `driver.update(object, id, patch plus updated_at, { preserveAudit: true })` (mail-log-body-migration.ts:247-250). The patch holds only the column or columns the planner changed.
  - SqlDriver keeps a supplied `updated_at` exactly when `preserveAudit` is true and the value is non-null (sql-driver.ts:8568-8570, applied at :8819). Otherwise it issues the patch by id only (:8805-8843). The contract says the same (driver.zod.ts:80-88).
  - When `updated_at` is null, the write omits `preserveAudit` and the driver would stamp now. That branch is not reached on an archived row: the Archiver's `upsert` stamps a null `updated_at` (sql-driver.ts:8554-8558).
  - The integration test reads both stores raw (`SELECT *` through its own better-sqlite3 connection, test:212-219). It compares every column except the two copy columns, `updated_at` included (test:306-313). On SQLite this is a byte-level proof.
- **Idempotent: yes.** A masked copy plans to null. This is pinned by the unit re-run (rewritten 0, rows deep-equal) and by integration case 3.
- **Edge cases: handled.**
  - *No table yet:* `isMissingTableError(e, object)`, with the object named, reads as no rows (:243).
  - *Any other refused read:* it counts one failure, warns, and stops that table (:291-300). The command then exits 1.
  - *Pagination:* keyset on `id`, with `$gt` and a limit of 500 (:280-329). The unit test pages at size 2 over 4 rows.
  - *Partial runs:* each write is one single-row update. An interrupted run leaves whole rows done and the rest for an idempotent re-run. No row is half-written.
- **Target: only the archive driver, only the two copy tables.**
  - `engine.getDriverByName(to)` (audit-mail-bodies.ts:283) reads the same `drivers` map that `engine.datasource(name)` reads (engine.ts:21491-21493 and :21671-21677). That is what the Archiver resolves its target with (lifecycle-service.ts:1344).
  - `to` comes from the registered object's `lifecycle.archive.to` (audit-mail-bodies.ts:274-279). The sweep reads the same field (`obj.lifecycle`, lifecycle-service.ts:738); governance overrides only windows, never `to` (:893-900).
  - The table list is fixed, and `objects` can only narrow it (mail-log-body-migration.ts:266, :276). No caller can aim the runner at another object. It reaches the hot store only if a deployment registers its hot driver under the archive's name.
  - The CLI boot never sweeps (`armLifecycleSweep: false`, schema-migrate.ts:1235-1238). So connecting the archive cannot make the CLI itself move rows.

**2. The CLI**

- **Shape: kept.**
  - The flags are unchanged from the base: `database-url`, `apply`, `yes`, `force` and `json` (audit-mail-bodies.ts:132-147).
  - The occupancy refusal, the `--yes` prompt and the JSON `confirmation_required` error are unchanged (:167-210).
  - Neither the base nor the head has a backup-attestation flag, so there was none to keep or lose.
- **Dry run: writes nothing to either store.**
  - The runner skips every write unless `apply` is set (mail-log-body-migration.ts:310).
  - The boot keeps `deferSchemaDdl` and `readOnlyProbe` (audit-mail-bodies.ts:231). The declared-datasource publisher inherits `readOnlyProbe` (schema-migrate.ts:649-657, :1351), so an absent SQLite archive opens empty in memory and is not created.
  - The runtime-row probe is a read (audit-mail-bodies.ts:48-62).
- **How targets are found.**
  - The command reads every copy table's declared `lifecycle.archive.to` (:274-279). Only `sys_audit_log` declares one; `sys_activity` is telemetry (sys-activity.object.ts:29-34).
  - When no driver is registered under `to`, it probes `sys_metadata` for `{ type: 'datasource', name, state: 'active' }` (:55). That is the filter `os serve`'s rehydration reads (datasource-admin-plugin.ts:130).
  - A row found reads `not-connected` and exits 1. A refused probe reads `unknown` and exits 1. Neither reads `none` and exits 0.
  - **But `none` is also the reading** for three cases where an archive exists: a declared archive this boot failed to connect, a declared archive the CLI's connect policy refused, and an archive a host registers outside the stack config. See B1 and B2.
- **`--json`: a widening.** The old keys `database`, `apply`, `report` and `duration` are kept, and one key, `archive`, is added (:301). `report` is still the hot runner's report, unchanged.
- **Nothing printed carries a body.**
  - The new lines print only datasource names, object names and counts (:314-340).
  - A runner warn line carries an error message. For a write, its bindings are the already-masked patch (mail-log-body-migration.ts:318-323). For a read, they are object names and an id.
  - Integration case 5 asserts that none of the five runs printed the sentinel.
- **`exitOneShotCommand`: clean exit.**
  - `run()` awaits `mask()` and then `exitOneShotCommand(process.exitCode or 0)` (audit-mail-bodies.ts:156-159). This is the pattern of plan.ts:132 and apply.ts:154.
  - `stack.shutdown()` runs in `finally` (:363-365).
  - The failure paths exit through oclif's `handle()`, which exits after its report (bin/run.js:186-190, :258).

**3. The future-archived rows claim: true.**

- The Archiver copies verbatim, with no hook in between: `cold.upsert(object, row, ['id'])` (lifecycle-service.ts:1501-1503). So a hot copy masked before it moves arrives masked.
- One invocation runs the hot half and then the archive half. A row the sweep moves before the hot half reaches it is already in the archive when the archive half starts. The operator therefore needs no ordering against the sweep.
- **Case 4 is a real proof of the mechanism** (test:327-332). The young copy masked hot by `--apply` (case 2: hot clear 0) is aged and moved by a second real sweep. It lands among 4 archive rows, with 0 clear.
- **The docs say this plainly:** "A hot copy masked first is archived masked" (cli.mdx:1515-1517).
- **They do not mention the sweep schedule.** A live server sweeps hourly, on an in-process timer, not a cron job (`DEFAULT_LIFECYCLE_SWEEP_MS`, lifecycle-service.ts:81, :512-519). See B6 for the narrow race this leaves.

**4. Tests**

- **Real Archiver, real driver.** The integration test runs `lifecycle.sweep()` (test:142) over a real SqlDriver on better-sqlite3 in both stores. The CLI is spawned from source (test:59, :191-209).
- **Counts and booleans: mostly.** Cases 2 and 3 also compare non-body columns and whole masked rows with `toEqual` (test:311, :314, :324). On failure those would print row contents. The fixtures are sentinels, so this is harmless (B8).
- **Ablation reproduces by reading.** With the lookup removed, the fixture falls to the runtime-row probe and reads `none`. Cases 1 to 4 then fail and cases 0, 5 and 6 pass. That is 4 red and 3 green, as the dev reported.
- **Positive control: present.** Case 1 asserts hot to-mask 1, and case 2 asserts hot clear 0 (test:290, :305).
- **Gaps.**
  - Case 1's "writes nothing" check reads `archivedBefore`, a snapshot taken before the dry run (test:244-246, :297). As a dry-run pin it is vacuous (B5).
  - No case declares an archive that fails to connect (B1).
- **Unit tests are meaningful** (mail-log-body-migration.test.ts:271-357). They use a real SqliteWasmDriver provisioned as the Archiver does. They cover the dry run; apply with page size 2, other-column equality and a deep-equal re-run; the missing table; and the refused read.

**5. Docs and changeset**

- **cli.mdx, partly matching.**
  - The examples, flags, and the `examined`, `not-connected` and `unknown` rows match the code, exit codes included (cli.mdx:1535, :1537-1538 against audit-mail-bodies.ts:293-297).
  - The `none` row (cli.mdx:1536) is false in the B1 and B2 cases. So is "so it reaches an archive declared there" (:1519-1520).
  - The command-table row says "Covers the `archive` datasource" (:1207). That holds only within B1 and B2's limits.
- **Changeset, sentence by sentence.**
  - *True:*
    - The 18.0.0 command was hot-only.
    - The lifecycle values match sys-audit-log.object.ts:36-40.
    - The Archiver copies verbatim, then deletes hot.
    - Clear bodies stay in the archive for as long as it keeps them.
    - The engine never routes `sys_audit_log` to the archive.
    - The command runs the hot half first, then the archive run in the same mode through the archive's driver.
    - `sys_activity` declares no archive.
    - Every other column is kept, `updated_at` included.
    - The run is idempotent and reports counts only.
    - A hot copy masked first is archived masked.
    - An archive is declared with `autoConnect: true` (gate (c), datasource-connection-service.ts:302).
    - A runtime-row archive reads `not-connected` and exits 1.
    - The `--json` `archive` entry shape and its four statuses match, and `report` is unchanged.
    - The export list matches index.ts:76-90.
  - *Not true as written:* "The command now connects the datasources the stack config declares, as `os serve` does."
    - It connects managed declarations only (`MANAGED_DATASOURCES_ONLY`, schema-migrate.ts:615-624).
    - An archive declared with `autoConnect: true` that fails to connect is left unconnected. The command then reads `none` (B1).
    - A fail-fast declaration that cannot connect now fails the run, and the changeset does not say so (B3).
- **No narrowing.** No export of `@objectstack/plugin-audit` is removed or renamed. The type-export line is split, and both old types are kept. The options parameter of `migrateMailLogBodyCopies` is a superset of the old literal type.

**6. Census**

- **Generated region and counts file: consistent with a regeneration.**
  - The gate runs `check-tenant-audit-census.mjs --self-test` and the check itself (lint.yml:2004-2008, inside the job named "Lint · repo & tooling gates"). That job is green on the head. Check A compares the committed region with a fresh run.
  - The new row reads `mail-log-body-migration.ts`, `update`, `object`, `undecidable`, `options unreadable`. That is what the generator gives a non-literal options argument (tenant-audit-census.mjs:1405-1421) together with a run-time object name.
  - Every figure that moved is +1 on a count the one new site moves.
  - The `39fc914f7` measurement stamp is the regeneration commit's parent. It sits in the generated region and is required to be present, not compared (check-tenant-audit-census.mjs:512, :524-554).
- **Prose: 11 number-only edits, each +1.**
  - Ten match enforced patterns (check-tenant-audit-census.mjs:289-400): mdx line 125 (two), lines 153-154 (two), line 190, line 192 (two), line 193, line 210's population, and line 214.
  - The eleventh is line 210's "93" to "94", which no pattern checks. It is true against the census's own 94.
  - "(56%)" is still right: 131 of 233.
- **Posture: accurate.**
  - The method is `update`.
  - The object is an arrow-function parameter, so it is chosen at run time.
  - Tenancy reads undecidable, and in fact `sys_audit_log` declares `tenant: false` (sys-audit-log.object.ts:31).
  - The options argument is a ternary, so it is unreadable.
- **No cross-tenant door.**
  - The runner acquires nothing. It acts on a driver its caller already holds, and that driver can already write anything.
  - It can only write `SECRET_MASK` over two body keys, inside the fixed copy columns of mail-log copies.
  - Its only caller is the CLI command (audit-mail-bodies.ts:285). No route, hook or plugin reaches it.
  - The ledger has no tenant column for a fence to key on. Masking every organization's copies is the purpose, as amendment 2 point 3 says.

**7. `schema-migrate.ts` comment: comment-only, and true.** The edit at :1172-1181 touches comment lines only. The four callers it names are exactly the four non-test callers: plan.ts:193, apply.ts:225, unmapped-columns.ts:303 and audit-mail-bodies.ts:230.

### ② Semver level

**`minor` for both packages is right, and so is `Clause-②: yes (widening)`.**

- plugin-audit adds `migrateArchivedMailLogBodyCopies`, three types, and an optional `objects` option.
- The CLI's `--json` document gains `archive` and keeps every old key.
- Nothing authorable is removed or renamed. AGENTS.md:1087-1092 defines a narrowing as the removal or rename of a spec key, an export or a config field.

**Seat point (1): the boot behaviour change.**

- *What changed:* the command now connects declared datasources. Before, it never tried, because no connection publisher was composed (schema-migrate.ts:600-605). A bound, mapped or boot-critical declaration that cannot connect now fails the command's boot with exit 1, where the run used to pass.
- *Precedent:* that is the verdict `os serve`, `os migrate plan` and `os migrate apply` already give, and it keeps the `OS_ALLOW_DRIVER_CONNECT_FAILURE` escape (datasource-connection-service.ts:953, :1019).
- *Judgment:* I do not read it as a Clause-② narrowing, since no authorable surface narrows. `minor` stands.
- *But:* the changeset does not state this consequence and owes one line (B3).
- The PR body's sentence on it ("A declared datasource that fails to connect therefore fails the command's boot") is true only for fail-fast declarations. It is false for the `autoConnect`-only archive (B1).
- The new exit 1 on `not-connected` and `unknown` is the fix itself, and the changeset states it.

### ③ Boundary flags

**B1 (BLOCKING): an under-mask reported clean, and false docs sentences.** A declared archive that this boot does not connect reads `none` and exits 0.

- *Why the connect fails silently:*
  - An archive declaration is addressed only by gate (c), `autoConnect: true`. "Gate (c) is not a fail-fast trigger" (datasource-connection-service.ts:290, :302).
  - So `handleFailure` finds no cause, logs "degrading (datasource left unconnected)" and returns without throwing (:968-1015). `connectDeclared` throws only on a fatal verdict (:376-397).
- *What the CLI then reports:*
  - With no driver, it falls to the runtime-row probe (audit-mail-bodies.ts:283-291). A config-declared archive has no such row, so the reading is `none`.
  - It prints "none on this deployment — nothing archived, nothing to mask" (:323) and exits 0. In `--json` the entry reads `status: 'none'`.
- *A second trigger:*
  - The CLI's connect policy refuses a non-managed `schemaMode` (`skipped-policy`, schema-migrate.ts:615-624, datasource-connection-service.ts:563-569).
  - `os serve` connects such a datasource under gate (a) (:301), so the Archiver fills it. The CLI then reads `none` the same way.
- *Why this matters for a p1 fix:* an operator who runs the command where the archive is unreachable gets a clean exit 0. Missing credentials or a different network segment are enough. Meanwhile the archive keeps clear reset, verification, magic-link and invitation bodies for up to 7 years.
- *False sentences:*
  - cli.mdx:1536 says `none` means "No such datasource … so nothing was archived".
  - cli.mdx:1519-1520 says "so it reaches an archive declared there".
  - The changeset says it "connects the datasources the stack config declares, as `os serve` does".
  - The class header promises "Absence is loud" (audit-mail-bodies.ts:114-119).
- **Smallest honest fix:**
  1. In the no-driver branch (:290-291), read the connection service's retained verdicts before the runtime-row probe, by `listConnectionStates()`, the way `findDeclaredDatasourceDrivers` does (schema-migrate.ts:690-697). If a declaration named `to` is addressed by gate D2 but not `available`, report `not-connected`, with its retained reason, and exit 1.
  2. Keep `none` only for an unaddressed declaration or no declaration at all. In both cases `os serve` does not connect it either, so the Archiver held every row hot.
  3. Add one integration case: a declared `autoConnect: true` archive that cannot connect must read `not-connected` and exit 1.

**B2 (BLOCKING): a false docs sentence, and the operator is not told (seat point 2).** A host-registered archive reads `none` and exits 0.

- *The case:* a host plugin publishes a `driver.archive` service, for example through `DriverPlugin` (runtime/src/driver-plugin.ts:39-41, adopted at objectql/src/plugin.ts:1060-1076). The CLI boot does not compose that host, so the command reads `none` and exits 0 while the archive holds clear bodies.
- *Where it is disclosed:* only in the PR body's Acceptance notes, which do not ship. cli.mdx, the changeset, the command's description (:120-124) and its `none` line (:323) all say nothing of it. cli.mdx:1536's "so nothing was archived" is false for this case.
- *Blocking for a p1 security fix:* yes. The shipped docs and output state a conclusion the code cannot know.
- **Smallest honest fix: text only**, since this boot cannot detect a host it does not compose. Reword the `none` output line, the cli.mdx `none` row and the changeset to say what was checked: no datasource of that name is declared and connected on this boot, and no active runtime row names one. Drop "so nothing was archived". State that an archive a host registers in code outside the stack config is not reached, and must be declared in the stack config's `datasources`, with `autoConnect: true`, to be masked. This rewording also serves B1's `none`.

**B3 (non-blocking, owed in the same pass): the changeset omits the boot consequence (seat point 1).** Add one line: a bound, mapped or boot-critical declared datasource that cannot connect now fails the command's boot with exit 1, as on `os serve`. Name the `OS_ALLOW_DRIVER_CONNECT_FAILURE` escape. This is not a Clause-② narrowing (see ②).

**B4 (non-blocking, pre-existing): a contradicted sentence next to the new text.** cli.mdx:1503-1506 says the copies "age out with each table's retention (... 90 for the audit log)".
